n: Joseph Smith called this revelation a prayer. It opens with a mighty heavenly voice echoing John the Baptist and Isaiah: prepare the way of the Lord and make his paths straight.

f.w: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight

n: The keys—priesthood authority to direct God’s kingdom—are on earth again. From here the gospel will roll forth like the stone in Daniel’s vision, cut from the mountain without hands, until it fills the whole earth.

f.w: The keys of the kingdom of God are committed unto man
the stone which is cut out of the mountain without hands

n: The voice cries again: prepare for the Lord, prepare the Lamb’s wedding supper, and be ready for the Bridegroom—Christ.
Pray to the Lord, call on his holy name, and tell the world about his wonderful works.

f.w: make known his wonderful works among the people

n: Pray that God’s kingdom spreads across the earth so people can be ready when the Son of Man comes in glory to meet the kingdom set up on earth.

f.w: to meet the kingdom of God which is set up on the earth
f.g: The Church on earth (kingdom of God) prepares for the Millennial reign (kingdom of heaven).

n: The prayer ends echoing the Lord’s Prayer: may God’s kingdom go forth so heaven’s kingdom can come, and God be glorified on earth as in heaven.

f.w: that the kingdom of heaven may come
